chunks: Ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a Muslim who killed a dhimmi. He said: "This is a grave matter that people would not bear, so let him give his family the blood-money of a Muslim, so that he may be deterred from killing the people of al-Sawad and from killing the dhimmi."

Then he said: "If a Muslim were to become angry with a dhimmi and wanted to kill him, take his land, and pay his family eight hundred dirhams, then killing among the dhimmis would become frequent. Whoever kills a dhimmi wrongfully, then it is indeed forbidden for the Muslim to kill a dhimmi unlawfully so long as he accepts the jizyah, pays it, and does not deny it."

As for the narration of Abi Basir specifically, we have narrated from him that their blood-money is eight hundred dirhams, like the rest of the reports. As for what his report included regarding a distinction between the Jews, the Christians, and the Magians, he also narrated that there is no distinction between them and that they are equal in blood-money. Others also narrated that, and we have already presented the reports concerning that; and what he narrated further clarifies it:

key_terms.أَهْلِهِ: his family or heirs entitled to receive compensation
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: the legally assessed indemnity for homicide
key_terms.الْجِزْيَةِ: the tribute paid by a protected non-Muslim under covenant
key_terms.دِيَةَ: blood-money paid as legal compensation for wrongful killing
key_terms.ذِمِّيًّا: a non-Muslim under Muslim protection and covenant

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on a Muslim who kills a dhimmi?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling concerning a Muslim who kills a dhimmi and stresses the seriousness of the crime. It indicates a deterrent legal approach to protect dhimmis from wrongful killing and affirms the unlawfulness of killing one who lives under covenant and pays the jizyah.
